statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail holds the watch floor at 20% on contained two-sided overnight structure, while Stress stays high at 79% on multi-decade Treasury yield highs, a sharply higher oil settlement and the September payrolls release later today.
recommendation: Tail remains below the 25% block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields WATCH and yellow. The flagged danger window spans the 12:30Z September payrolls release through the first US cash hour, ending 14:30Z. Narrow evidence-based windows are preferred over a broad session-wide state because no persistent one-way NQ structure is observed.
headline: NQ holds a contained overnight band ahead of September payrolls; Tail 20%, Stress 79%
body: NQ futures trade 30,875.75 (+0.37%) inside an unchanged overnight band of 30,760.25-30,920.00. Price retraced roughly 88 points from the 30,920.00 overnight high, has recovered part of that move and has not retaken the high, leaving a two-sided range of about 0.5%. Cash NDX closed Thursday at 30,501.56 (+0.31%, range 30,274.65-30,616.24) and VIX is 16.39 after decaying from a 17.59 session high. The dominant feature of the environment is the long end of the US curve: the 10-year reached 5.3445% on Thursday, its highest since April 2002, and the 30-year 5.6702%, the highest since July 2002, following the largest quarterly 10-year advance since 1994. H.15 for September 30 shows the 2-year at 4.88%, the 10-year at 5.29% and the federal funds effective rate at 3.88%. Dallas Fed President Logan stated on October 1 that the target range needs to rise an additional 50 basis points or more. Oil settled sharply higher, with Brent December at $102.31 (+4.37%) and WTI $92.87 (+2.71%), after reports that Chinese refiners suspended oil-product exports beyond Hong Kong and Macau and that the US is sending a third aircraft carrier and up to 10,000 additional troops to the Middle East amid the US-Iran conflict. September payrolls, the unemployment rate and average hourly earnings release at 12:30Z, with consensus near 89-90K against 162K prior, unemployment seen at 4.1% and earnings at +0.3% month over month; roughly 75% of market-implied probability sits on unchanged rates this month. That stack is a Stress and Confidence input rather than a Tail input until an actual price path is observed: cross-asset signals currently conflict, with yields and oil higher while equity volatility stays contained and NDX closed higher. Tail therefore holds the watch floor at 20%. The shared Finviz context file was stale, generated 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z with collectionStatus partial, so it was excluded and this assessment rests on independent primary-source research; that single completeness gap is the only reason Confidence is not higher than 88%.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours were continuously assessed with no unavailable slots. Tail drifted from 21% up to a single 25% print in the 06:00Z hour on a brief trend-up reading, then returned to the 20-24% watch band and settled at 20% for most of the US session and the overnight hours. Stress climbed steadily from 70% to 79% as the long end of the US curve pushed to multi-decade highs and oil settled sharply higher, with a mid-session peak of 78% around the 14:00Z and 15:00Z hours. Confidence held at 87-89% throughout. The dominant mode was mixed except for the 05:00Z and 06:00Z trend-up readings.
outlookSummary: The base case is continued two-sided rotation inside the overnight band through the Asian and European hours, with Tail held at the 20-22% watch floor and Stress in the high band. The 12:30Z September payrolls release and the overlapping 13:30Z US cash open form the widest-variance window of the forecast: Stress reaches the extreme band at 86-87% and Tail steps to 24%, still below the 25% block threshold, because no post-release price path is observed at publication. From the second US cash hour the base case is volatility decay as the release is absorbed, returning Tail to 20% and Stress to the mid-70s. CME equity futures reach the Friday 21:00Z weekly halt, after which no price path can form; Confidence steps down to 73-80% for the closed hours to reflect the absence of live evidence rather than any change in the assessment, and the watch floor is retained for Sunday reopen-gap risk from unresolved US-Iran escalation.
